Gluon's built-in catalog: facts about each model, not configuration. The **Id** is what the intake agent proposes and `--launch --model` takes; the connection columns are the id each connection's API or plan uses (— : not served there). Which of these the intake agent may propose is decided per machine by a check (`gluon doctor`); how it decides is in [Connections](../guides/connections.md#how-gluon-decides-a-model-is-reachable).

## Claude Code

Anthropic's own harness. Strongest general coding agent; best for multi-file features, debugging and refactors.

- Binary: `claude` (Anthropic)
- Connections: Claude plan (subscription), Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, OpenRouter
- Modes besides build: `explore`: supported; `plan`: supported

| Model | Id | Claude plan | Anthropic | Amazon Bedrock | OpenRouter | Efforts | Default effort | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Haiku 5.5 | `haiku` | `haiku` | `claude-haiku-5-5` | `global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5` | `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | `medium` | fast and cheap; small, well-specified edits |
| Sonnet 5.5 | `sonnet` | `sonnet` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | `high` | strong and mid-priced; default for most everyday tasks |
| Opus 5.5 | `opus` | `opus` | `claude-opus-5-5` | `global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5` | `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | `medium` | most capable, expensive; hard debugging, design, large changes |
| Fable 5.1 | `fable` | `fable` | `claude-fable-5-1` | `global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1` | `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | `high` | frontier model, most expensive; the hardest, longest tasks |

Install (official methods, the vendor's recommended first; Gluon shows the command and runs it only on an explicit "Run it"):

| Where | Command | Downloads from | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux, macOS, WSL | `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh \| bash` | claude.ai |  |
| Windows | `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 \| iex` | claude.ai |  |

## Codex

OpenAI's harness. Strong at well-specified implementation work and careful, test-driven changes.

- Binary: `codex` (OpenAI)
- Connections: ChatGPT plan (subscription), OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, OpenRouter
- Modes besides build: `explore`: supported; `plan`: typed as `/plan` once the agent is up

| Model | Id | ChatGPT plan | OpenAI | Amazon Bedrock | OpenRouter | Efforts | Default effort | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPT-6 Luna | `gpt-6-luna` | `gpt-6-luna` | `gpt-6-luna` | `global.openai.gpt-6-luna` | `openai/gpt-6-luna` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` | `high` | fast and cheap; small, well-specified edits |
| GPT-6.1 Sol | `gpt-6.1-sol` | `gpt-6.1-sol` | `gpt-6.1-sol` | `global.openai.gpt-6.1-sol` | `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` | `medium` | strong and mid-priced; everyday implementation work |
| GPT-6 Astra | `gpt-6-astra` | `gpt-6-astra` | `gpt-6-astra` | `global.openai.gpt-6-astra` | `openai/gpt-6-astra` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` | `medium` | most capable, expensive; hard, ambiguous work |

Install (official methods, the vendor's recommended first; Gluon shows the command and runs it only on an explicit "Run it"):

| Where | Command | Downloads from | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux, macOS, WSL | `curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh \| sh` | chatgpt.com |  |
| Linux, macOS, WSL | `npm install -g @openai/codex` | registry.npmjs.org |  |
| Windows | `irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 \| iex` | chatgpt.com |  |

## Antigravity

Google's harness on Gemini. Fast and cheap; good for well-scoped edits and quick fixes.

- Binary: `agy` (Google)
- Connections: Google account (subscription), Gemini API
- Modes besides build: `explore`: plan mode; `plan`: supported

| Model | Id | Google account | Gemini API | Efforts | Default effort | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gemini 3.8 Flash | `gemini-3.8-flash` | `gemini-3.8-flash` | `gemini-3.8-flash` | `low`, `medium`, `high` | `high` | fast Gemini; good quality at a low price |

## OpenCode

Open-source harness on OpenRouter or the OpenCode Go plan. Good for well-scoped tasks when an open or cheaper model is enough.

- Binary: `opencode` (OpenCode)
- Connections: OpenRouter, OpenCode Go plan
- Modes besides build: `explore`: supported; `plan`: supported

| Model | Id | OpenRouter | OpenCode Go plan | Efforts | Default effort | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek Flash | `deepseek-flash` | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `low`, `high`, `max` | `max` | very cheap and fast; small, mechanical edits (follows the latest DeepSeek Flash: V4.1 today); follows the latest release (deepseek-v4.1-flash today) |
| Muse Spark 1.3 | `muse-spark-1.3` | `meta/muse-spark-1.3` | — | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | `max` | Meta's model; capable generalist |
| Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor | `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | `meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` | `xhigh` | Meta's coding-tuned variant, very cheap; Meta receives the session's code and prompts; opt-in: `allow_muse_contributor` in routing.yaml; Meta receives the session's code and prompts |

Install (official methods, the vendor's recommended first; Gluon shows the command and runs it only on an explicit "Run it"):

| Where | Command | Downloads from | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux, macOS, WSL | `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install \| bash` | opencode.ai |  |
| Linux, macOS, WSL | `npm install -g @opencode/cli` | registry.npmjs.org |  |
| Windows | `npm install -g @opencode/cli` | registry.npmjs.org |  |

## Kimi Code

Moonshot AI's harness on Kimi K3 and K2.7 Code, on a Moonshot or OpenRouter API key, or the Kimi Code plan. Good for long agentic coding tasks at a modest price.

- Binary: `kimi` (Moonshot AI)
- Connections: Kimi Code plan (subscription), Moonshot AI, OpenRouter
- Modes besides build: `explore`: unavailable (its interactive mode ignores an agent file, so no flag can take its writing and shell tools away; use plan mode, or build); `plan`: supported

| Model | Id | Kimi Code plan | Moonshot AI | OpenRouter | Efforts | Default effort | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kimi K2.7 Code | `kimi-k2.7-code` | — | `kimi-k2.7-code` | `moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code` | none | — | Moonshot's coding model; cheap, good for well-scoped coding tasks (not on the plan) |
| Kimi K3 | `kimi-k3` | `k3` | `kimi-k3` | `moonshotai/kimi-k3` | `low`, `high`, `max` (Kimi Code plan only) | `high` | Moonshot's flagship; long agentic coding tasks, 1M context |

Install (official methods, the vendor's recommended first; Gluon shows the command and runs it only on an explicit "Run it"):

| Where | Command | Downloads from | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux, macOS, WSL | `curl -fsSL https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.sh \| bash` | code.kimi.com | Linux needs glibc: the installer refuses Alpine (musl). It adds kimi to your shell profile's PATH and renames an old Python `kimi-cli` on PATH to `kimi-legacy`. |
| Windows | `irm https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.ps1 \| iex` | code.kimi.com | Needs Git for Windows (kimi's shell). It renames an old Python `kimi-cli` on PATH to `kimi-legacy`. |
